title: Number of Great Partitions
summary: Given an array nums consisting of positive integers and an integer k, partition the array into two ordered groups such that the sum of the elements in each group is at least k.
statement: Given an array nums consisting of positive integers and an integer k, partition the array into two ordered groups such that the sum of the elements in each group is at least k. Return the number of distinct great partitions, where two partitions are considered distinct if at least one element is in a different group. Since the result can be large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Assign every positive array element to exactly one of two labeled groups.
A partition is great when both group sums are at least k.
Return the number of assignments modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Start with all 2^n labeled assignments and subtract assignments with a group sum below k.
When total sum is at least 2k, the events that either group is too small are disjoint and symmetric.
Use descending one-dimensional subset-sum DP to count subsets for every sum from zero through k-1.
Twice the number of small-sum subsets is exactly the number of bad labeled assignments; if total is below 2k no great partition exists.
editorial: Twice the number of small-sum subsets is exactly the number of bad labeled assignments; if total is below 2k no great partition exists.

tests.explanation: Exactly six labeled assignments leave both group sums at least four.
Every split leaves one group below four, so the answer is zero.
